definition: Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (RCRA) is the title for the 1976 federal environmental law that substantially amended the Solid Waste Disposal Act and established a national framework for managing solid and hazardous waste. The RCRA is codified at 42 U.S.C. § 6901 et seq. The Act authorizes the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) to establish and enforce federal requirements governing waste management programs. The RCRA uses "solid waste" as a legal term, not merely a description of physical form. Under 42 U.S.C. § 6903, solid waste can include discarded material in solid, liquid, semisolid, or contained gaseous form. The RCRA defines "hazardous waste" as solid waste that, because of its quantity, concentration, or characteristics, may cause or significantly contribute to, increased mortality or to serious irreversible or incapacitating reversible illness, or pose a substantial present or potential hazard if it is improperly managed. The EPA implements the RCRA through regulations principally codified in Title 40 of the Code of Federal Regulations (CFR). The RCRA is divided into statutory Subtitles, including Subtitle C (Subchapter III, Hazardous Waste Management), Subtitle D (Subchapter IV, Solid Waste Disposal), and Subtitle I (Subchapter IX, Regulation of Underground Storage Tanks). These statutory Subtitles should be distinguished from the parts and subparts of the CFR that contain EPA's implementing regulations. Subchapter III (42 U.S.C. §§ 6921–6939g) creates the principal hazardous-waste program. It regulates waste from generation through transportation, treatment, storage, and disposal, often known as "cradle-to-grave" management. The system includes rules for identifying hazardous waste; duties for generators and transporters; manifests used to track shipments; operating and permitting standards for treatment, storage, and disposal facilities; land-disposal restrictions; enforcement; and corrective action for certain releases. Subchapter IV (42 U.S.C. §§ 6941–6949a) addresses nonhazardous solid waste.
